data: 10/10, beautiful and amazing game that is well worth the price
Amazing visual, amazing music, amazing experience, amazing journey
Great game with a great story
This game is wonderful, great music, amazing atmosphere, and addictive gameplay
Overall, 10/10 definitely would recommend, especially if you play it with friends
For me there is literally nothing interesting here, the story is non-existent, i didn't find the visuals impressive and the game mechanics are laughable

Journey is mostly an experience more than a game, it does have game aspects like collectables which also serve to either upgrade your scarf (flying ability) or hint at some backstory. And it has a few stealth sections, but they aren't really punishing you too harshly if you get seen, and some very mild puzzles in a few areas and 'platforming'.

It's not for everyone, but it's a great experience to me. Soundtrack is fantastic, visuals are still beautiful despite being a game made for the PS3. Art design makes all the difference.

Wow! What a game! What a piece of art! Its so quiet yet says so much. So intuitive! So smooth! Really satisfying. I got very involved and It took me on a emotional roller coaster. Definitely one of the best games ive ever played! Recommended!

One of my favorite games. Simple yet full of depth and replayability.

Great soundtrack, absolutely nails the atmosphere and captures my curiosity. The designs and lore are inspired by various cultures from around the world, especially ancient Sumer in Mesopotamia.

Worth playing again and again if you enjoy stuff like this.

While I still recommend the game and found it beautiful some things annoyed me. The game is easy and all, but the lack of a tutorial is annoying because I didn't want to read tips nor see gameplays before playing and I spent a lot of time wandering around trying to figure out wtf I was supposed to do. Then I saw another "copy" of me and thought "hey, cool, there's a npc to guide my noob ass" to find out that was an actual player and all other dudes I found along the way were other players too lol no wonder they simply vanished after a while and then at the end I started freezing to death thinking that was how I was gonna end and I got an achievement. I know you are supposed to play again and better since you now know what to expect but I probably won't do it anytime soon...

This game fell within me with a good reputation, although it remembered me to Hollow Knight at least the beginning, a faceless creature without any context on why or what are you doing there.

No need to say I didn't think this was multiplayer, so I was just roaming around when I found another creature like mine, I decided to tag along thinking it was a bot, needless to say it wasn't and I noticed later on, this experience may lack action or any other general game characteristics but my god, is it beautiful

Thanks a lot Skeletor, thanks for making my experience this unique, I don't know if you'll read this, but just to thank you and say sorry, my wifi turned off at the end xd

A beautiful little game that understands exactly what it wants to be.

I finished Journey in less than 2 hours and that felt like the perfect length. The gameplay is simple and forgiving, with no frustrating trial-and-error, no difficult jumps, and no need to repeat sections because of precise timing. You can simply keep moving forward and experience the journey.

For me, it felt like a metaphor for life itself: always moving toward some distant goal, represented by the mountain, while dealing with struggle along the way and occasionally being rewarded with genuinely beautiful moments. The music plays a huge part in making those moments work.

It is definitely more of an experience than a traditional game, but unlike some so-called artistic games, it never forgets to be enjoyable to actually play.

Short, atmospheric, meaningful and very well paced.

Played this with a friend, neither of us had played before and we didn't VC till after we had finished. Is a really cinematic and beautiful game. I suspect playing with a stranger would make the ending even more impactful but even with my friend I still found myself crying at the final scene.

this is not a game, this is an experience

you are climbing up a mountain, are you expecting celeste type of climbing? nope. you are meeting other players in real time, are you gonna battle it out to see who gets to keep on going? not at all. well what type of game is this? a game where you walk and go up, you meet other players and they cannot interact with you besides giving extra charge with the only way of communicating.

you might expect awesome realistic graphix since this was released on the playstation first but no, the models are simplistic, its mostly rocks, sand, snow and cloth. well are the textures good? abselutley. te way the game is structured you have to slow down, there are some things that might confuze most players but alot of places people get stuck are usaly where another player beforeyou usaly are

is there a language barrier between communicating? the only communication barrier is that there are no letters at all, just short and long notes causing one to just spam it. if you are expecting hundreads of players flocking this game? dont, i am writing this review after i am done with the game and i only met 3 other players and the player list is shown at the end of the credits

9/10

Damn, that was hell of a Journey for sure. 

I really like the dunes, the long scarf, the matchmaking and the journey itself, ending was le sadge, but very good game.
Great game - fun to play and nice to interact with other players - without the normal online 'complications' that come from voice chat etc. Works well streaming on Steam Link device too.

Journey's a classic for a reason. It's a very artsy game, with a gorgeous soundtrack, a story that's vague but compelling, and smooth, enjoyable gameplay. It's mostly very quiet and contemplative, best experienced without spoilers but still well worth playing if you've already seen it played.

I think it's worth expecting to get two playthroughs, and if you enjoy mastering movement and completion there's a surprising amount of depth to the game's mechanics. Overall, a solid choice for someone who enjoys slower paced, story focused games.

I don't remember the last time I cried for a game, but here I cried again.
It's like watching a two-hour movie with stunning graphics and instrumental relaxing music, where the actor's destination is somewhere like heaven.

Never seen a game do this feature of "npcs" "companions". It felt so cute running around with another player and connecting through just in game movement and sounds. 10/10 best gaming experience ive had in a while. :)

Even if I completed the game in under 2 hours it is one of the most emotional games I've played. It's amazing how the game is able to tell a story with only visuals and music and not a single word. The soundtrack is unbelievably good and hits just the right time. I really like when I meet another player and experience the game together. Unfortunately that player left before the ending but the way it's executed is good that you can not see the name or communicate. The only thing you can do is make sounds to each other and it makes you care for that completely strange person. The end left me with a lot of thoughts and emotions. This is truly a masterpiece, it's a must play in my opinion.

One of my favourite games of all time. First played it on the PS3 and fell in love with the art styles and the music. Also love just coming across random people and only finding out who they are at the end. 100% recommend this game to EVERYONE

It's beautiful! The animations and the music really add to the game. It's not very difficult and i would say that it's more of a piece of art to be taken in and casually played than a fun, engaging game. I found 0 glitches or problems at all apart from a small pull on the camera in certain places, no doubt it wants you to see the view from the best angle. Almost every frame is as beautiful as the cover art. And before you dismiss it as boring, there are some really fun parts as well.

Loved it, the first game I've played in 15 years, amazing visuals, beautiful soundtrack, atmospheric, emotional, and relaxing.

Makes you want to start over immediately after you finish it.

Also it was great that I could play it with no issues on my very basic laptop with no graphics card.

Got it on a super sale. It's pretty darn short but it's a super memorable experience. I played almost the entire game with just one other person, communicating with them only through beeps. I won't forget you Femboy VI.

I don't know about others, but for me, this is the most relaxing game.
The soundtrack, the gameplay, the environment, even the fact that you can meet other players but the only thing that you can do is help them... all of them are brilliant.
The only bad side is that it finishes too fast, but, well, it can't have everything.

One of the most beautiful and memorable games I've ever played, definitely stays beautiful despite its age. It is like no other, and I love playing it alone but it's even more fun to be with someone, I met people along the way I won't forget.

As stunning and mesmerizing as it was in 2012. It hasn't aged a day.

This is a contemplative, bite-sized, extremely polished, minimalist adventure, with some of the most beautiful art direction and music ever created for a video game.

It's also one of the most universally recommendable games I've ever had the pleasure of playing, given how accessible and enjoyable the premise and execution are.

It encompasses every tone, from the most adventurous and liberating to the darkest and most terrifying.

And it never drags on. It never goes beyond what's necessary. Nothing is left out. It's just right .

I recommend playing it in one sitting, preferably without anyone else around so you can fully appreciate the introspection it evokes.

This is the kind of game you can categorize as "an experience," since it's so unique.

Do yourself a favor and just play it.
Wait until it's on sale. It's pretty short. Even going in expecting a walking sim, personally felt story and game play was a little underwhelming.

Journey is a calm, beautiful experience that focuses on emotion rather than challenge. The music, art style, and quiet storytelling work together to create something peaceful and meaningful. Meeting other players without words was surprisingly touching.

There isn’t much traditional gameplay, and it’s fairly short, but that’s part of its charm.

A game you don’t rush, you feel.
Recommended: Yes

This is a very chilled out game .. a calm and pleasant experience (apart from one bit not spoiling it for other players though) .. can be finished quite quickly or you can really take your time and explore every little bit .. after playing Sky on my tablet this was much easier to do on keyboard and thoroughly enjoyed it .. hope they do a cross between Journey and Sky (with none of the Sky monsters lol )
Journey's beauty lies not in what is said, but in what is left unsaid, creating a sanctuary for inner peace and reflection.

8/10

I wasn't sure what to expect from this game, but I had heard vaguely good things about it. I was pleasantly surprised with the atmospheric nature, the calming actions, and the puzzles were not very hard but it was still a very enjoyable experience, which lasted a little under 3 hours for me. It is a game I could see myself replaying from time to time. Definitely worth the price.

It's exactly the type of unique indie game that I love. Thanks for making it, ThatGameStudio!
Simple, yet the story was amazing. It takes a little bit to understand what your doing but once you do the story fully engulfs you.

I had a great time playing, I was so lucky as to have a person joining me through most of the trip so I wasn't entirely lost. And I'll need to play again to get all the achievements, but 10/10 would recommend giving it a go! You may have a bit of confusion in the beginning as to what to do, but it didn't take me long to figure it out.

Journey is a game unlike anything else I’ve experienced. From the moment I set foot on the endless sand dunes, I was instantly mesmerized by the game’s stunning and grandiose world. It’s hard not to admire the incredible graphics, where every landscape feels like a piece of art. The colors, the light, and the constant interplay between the sand and the wind create an atmosphere that’s both calming and mysterious. As much as I love the world and the emotional journey, I can’t help but feel the game could have been even more powerful with a deeper story. The minimalist design sometimes leaves you wanting more background or a more expansive narrative to engage with. While the symbolism is beautiful and open to interpretation, I would have appreciated a bit more substance in the plot and characters.
I made a friend and I don't know anything about them, but we had a great adventure. It was emotional. Goodbye friend.

the neurodivergent part of my brain loved the lil chirps back and forth between who you Journey with.. no words, none of the downs of socializing, just short and long chirps!! It's creative way to limit communication while keeping it fun. I'll play a couple more Journeys just for the chirps they're sm fun

Nice game, well thought out, with unexpected multiplayer mechanic (companion) that didn't require doing anything. Some elements of puzzle and hiding involved. Beautiful imagery. 90 minute play through if focusing on finishing. Worth it. What games should be more like.

Although the game is very short, enduring the journey that this game puts you through was enlightening. Everything about it - the landscape, soundtrack and ambience - were simple yet masterful.

I cannot recommend this title any more for those looking for a title with a beautiful aesthetic.

An amazing game. The perfect combination between music and gameplay. The soundtrack from Austin Wintory is out of this world.
I played it in Playstation 3 many years ago and I was amazed. How this game without a clear story and with a character without a name and without voice can drive to your tears.
At the end, when your character reaches the end of the pilgrimage I was completely moved.
You encounter some characters like yourself along the way. At the end I understood that there were other players playing at the same time like a multiplayer game. Thats a nice touch, I dont know if it was the same way in the PS3.
This is a must have experience. The only indy game that is between my top favourites games of all time.

This was one of the greatest gaming experiences I've had in probably a decade, generously. I knew the game was a cult hit but I'd never really looked into it.

Easily worth the price. The story, the music, the visuals were all spot on. It just felt like the golden age of gaming again; It's just fun, compelling, moving. The dumb joy you feel when you run into another player and just chirp like fools, or draw pictures at each other in the sand.

I felt intensely compelled to complete it and become a white scarf. So I did; First game I think I've wanted all the achievements on.

It truly was a Journey.
A friend guided me up the mountain, we wrote hearts in the snow to each other, and then walked into the end. Thank you Connor McCoolman.

One of the most unique and intriguing games I've played. The mysterious atmosphere, calming (and at times tense) music, and most importantly, the companionship, have a soothing effect. Wished it was longer though.

I dropped it for being too slow, but i guess thats exactly what the game needs to be. Its relaxing and beautiful, just not my thing, but if its relaxation youre looking for, it does scratch your brain
Loved this game but i wish i came across more players during my journey, had to play and beat the game twice to find someone :)

I'm not crying... YOU ARE!

Sadly the game crashed just after the credits, so no ending achievement for me, but at least its another reason to replay it.

Absolutely breathtakingly beautiful experience,

The Journey really is more then the destination.

This is certainty not for everyone. I would not recommend this unless it is on sale. The whole experience takes about an hour and a half long. While this does not account for achievement hunting, I know only a minority of people actually try to hunt for them. This does have a multiplayer aspect to it, that if you are unlucky on your first play-through. You wont even notice other players. I didn't until about midway through the game. Once I realized I was playing with another person the experience did improve significantly. The music is good, the visuals are awesome, and the story telling is very abstracted. Its told though visuals and leaves a lot open for interpretation. Its a very relaxing game with a very few moments of panic. While I would have recommenced this for everyone if the game was cheaper, I can not justice a 15$ price tag. Again, I would only suggest buying it if it were on sale.

This is a wonderful game that I've played every few years since it came out on the PS3. It is beautiful, emotional, creative, and has mostly relaxing game play. It is not a game for those of you looking for a challenge or competition. Playing with a random online friend can be an enjoyable way to connect with a stranger if the stranger has a play style that meshes well with yours. Unfortunately, too many times I've been paired online with someone that wants to rush through the game as if it is a speed-run contest rather than a cooperative undertaking, and this has ruined the experience for me. I support everyone being able play the game the way they want to, I just wish I could easily flip a switch in the game's options to make it a single player game. Hopefully, the developer will add a single-player mode to the options sometime soon, but that seems unlikely since the game has been out for over a decade. The good news is that you can force the game into single player mode by turning off your access to the internet. Thank you to ThatGameCompany and Annapurna for making and releasing a great and unique game. ... next your should make your Flower game Steam Deck verified; Flower, runs poorly on the Steam Deck.

most beautiful and intimate experience ive ever had with a video game. I played this game for the first time on the ps3 while on vacation in france when i was about 8 years old. I tried replaying it about a year ago but was too scared to ruin the nostalgia tinted memories i had of this game by playing it again. This night at around 4:30AM i very impulsively decided to give it another shot and man. this game touches your soul. its such a beautiful depiction of life, love and friendship in such a uniquely abstract world that feels so personal that it seems alive at times. pls do urself the favor of playing this if u havent , I cannot praise this piece of art enough.

It looks and sounds alright, but otherwise I don't get what's so magical about it. Occasionally for the briefest of moments the pace of the game picks up and then becomes slow and tedious again and in the end I was just waiting for it to end even though the whole thing only took about 2 hours.
Beautiful game. I had no idea it was multiplayer and it really added to the experience. Short but very sweet, Highly recommend this game to everyone.
Beautiful game following the trail to the summit. Game may have simple controls but it provides an experience that can be played through over and over again.

I had a long-distance friend who really loved this game. One day, she left all social media and I haven't been able to contact her in over three years. I wonder sometimes if she's ever come back to this game and if we've ever crossed paths. Wherever you are, I hope you're doing well.

Exceptional. The art style and music is very immersive. I highly enjoyed this relaxing experience and hey! those folks you meet while playing are actually more gamers! How cool is that? Very interesting proposal.

In terms of music, visuals, and themes, this is the singular most beautiful game you are likely to ever play. No combat. Just a journey and a metaphor. Absolutely beautiful from start to finish. The replay value is the journey and those you meet along the way. 10/10. An absolute masterpiece.

Wow, over 17k reviews at the time I'm writing this. Not much more can be said, Journey is an incredible game. But I feel that many Steam players are kinda missing out on some of it's best aspects.

1. Journey was meant to be played with a gamepad. Yes you *can* play with kb/mouse, but you won't be able to do any trick moves. Even the simplest trick like doing a faceplant requires spinning the left stick, which of course is impossible with a kb/mouse. Advanced tricks like boosting are also impossible without a gamepad.
2. Playing with friends *is* possible . You just need to work around the games matchmaking. Coordinating with a friend so you both enter the first game level (the bridge area) at the same time usually works.
3. There are secret exits to go outside the game's levels. All those areas in the game that you can see but can't reach, like the far off bridges and buildings. You can reach all those places. Journey is the only game I know of that has such a rich abundance of exploration out of the restricted/designed play area. You can spend hours and hours exploring, and every single level has it's secrets, though some require advanced flight techniques to access.

After you've played through a few times, you'll unlocked the white cloak. That's when Journey begins to open up like an oyster revealing it's pearl.

tldr.text: Very Positive (92%): the graphics and art are the main thing players love.
Few reviews complain, mostly about the story and characters.

details.text: Recent reviews sit at 85% positive, 7 points below the all-time score, so the recent dip is worth weighing for anyone buying now.
Players who stay with the game longer are the most positive group, while newer players still lean positive.
